Humanoids

Embodied AI unveils AIR, a wheeled humanoid with tendon-driven arms

The EPFL spinout puts motors in the torso to reduce arm mass and learns from operators; CE certification remains a 2027 target.

RoboticsTomorrow ↗6 November 2026English editorial summary
Story

Designed around factory work

Swiss company Embodied AI unveiled AIR on November 6 after about nine months of development. The EPFL spinout combines a human-like upper body with a wheeled base for flat industrial floors, targeting repetitive manipulation rather than bipedal locomotion.

Tendons reduce moving arm mass

Motors, gearboxes and electronics sit in the torso, transmitting motion through tendons to lighter, compliant arms. The company cites design work under ISO/TS 15066:2016, while CE certification is planned for 2027. That does not establish completed certification today.

Operators teach before autonomy expands

Deployment begins with human operation and recorded demonstrations. The company says autonomy typically follows in about a month, with operators available for difficult cases. It reports tests with unnamed major manufacturers and plans to scale production. The training period is a supplier claim, not a guarantee for every task.
